source_acquisition.search_note: The PDF explicitly links cmu-l3/ntp-toolkit/tree/hammer, hanwenzhu/LeanHammer-training, hanwenzhu/lean-premise-server, hanwenzhu/premise-selection, and JOSHCLUNE/LeanHammer. gh exact-title repository search returned hanwenzhu/premise-selection as the relevant candidate; gh tree inspection of all five default branches found no paper-specific plot*, figure*, visual*, table*, .tex, .tikz, .pgf, .svg, .ipynb, or style source. LeanHammer-training/scripts/print_results.py has a generic optional --plot Matplotlib helper but no matching Figure 1/table data or paper layout, so it is not recorded as an exact visual source.

paper_style.palette_strategy: Figure 1 uses a diagrams.net-like green/yellow/blue phase palette with black solid versus red dashed edges; all tables are monochrome black rules/text except the light-gray ✗ glyphs in Table 1.
paper_style.vector_raster_mix: PDF body text and all table rules are vector objects. Figure 1 is an embedded RGB raster XObject (1062 × 242 at 215 × 215 ppi) with a soft mask; there are no other figures.
paper_style.style_consistency: Captions and tables share a restrained serif/booktabs conference style and consistent one-decimal numeric treatment. Figure 1 labels use estimated sans-serif raster type, and table body size varies from about 8.44 to 8.97 pt; the functional type mismatch is visible but stable.

figures.label: Figure 1

caption.text: Figure 1: Overview of the LEANHAMMER pipeline. Phases that can neither fail nor produce a terminal proof are green, phases that can fail but cannot produce a terminal proof are yellow, and phases that can produce a terminal proof are blue. Black solid arrows indicate control flow, while red dashed arrows indicate the transfer of information between phases.

color.semantic_mapping: Green/yellow/blue fills and borders classify phases by failure and terminal-proof capability; black solid arrows are control flow and red dashed arrows are information transfer.

encodings.x: Pipeline stage/control-flow order from left to right
encodings.y: Branch layout: main upper path and Aesop lower branch
encodings.color: Green/yellow/blue phase capability classes; black versus red arrow color also separates edge semantics
encodings.shape: Rounded rectangles for phases; arrowheads on directed edges
encodings.line: Black solid control flow versus red dashed information transfer

figures.data_and_statistics: Conceptual method diagram; no quantitative observations or uncertainty. It contains 7 labeled phase nodes and 9 directed edges (7 black solid control-flow edges and 2 red dashed information-transfer edges).
figures.evidence_relation: p.3 §3.1 introduces the three hammer components; p.4 Figure 1 instantiates the unified LeanHammer pipeline. Tables 2–3 measure the resulting end-to-end proof rate, while Table 4 ablates related extraction/training components. The figure is structural evidence, not a performance estimate.
design_strengths: Cross-column overview combines stage order, branching, and two edge semantics.
Direct labels avoid a separate node legend.
Caption defines all three fill classes and both arrow classes.
design_weaknesses: The only figure is an embedded 215 ppi raster, so zoomed or printed text and arrows soften before the PDF body text.
Phase capability is primarily color-coded; the light fills are not robustly redundant in grayscale or for color-vision deficiency.
The red diagonal information edge and black diagonal control edge are close near the Aesop branch.
The diagram does not encode latency, failure counts, inputs/outputs, or uncertainty.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use one cross-column flow diagram for input, retrieval, branched reasoning, and reconstruction; place stage labels in nodes, distinguish control and information edges by line style, and define the visual key in the caption. Prefer vector export and add texture/shape redundancy when colors carry phase semantics.

tables.label: Table 1

caption.text: Table 1: Usability comparison of existing premise selection tools. Note that this is orthogonal to the quantitative performance comparisons (Table 2).

tables.uncertainty: Not applicable: ✓/✗ usability indicators have no numeric uncertainty, denominator, failure count, or interval encoding.
tables.data_and_statistics: Categorical usability matrix for ReProver, Lean Copilot, random forest, MePo, and LeanPremise across LM-based, Callable in Lean, and New premises. Cells are binary ✓/✗ indicators rather than measured performance.
tables.evidence_relation: p.6 §3.3.2 uses this table to separate interface/usability claims from the quantitative performance in Table 2. It supports the callable-in-Lean and new-premise method boundary; it is not an outcome comparison.
design_strengths: Three user-facing capability columns make a 4-column matrix fast to scan.
A horizontal group rule separates prior selectors from LeanPremise without vertical grid lines.
The caption explicitly states orthogonality to quantitative performance comparisons.
design_weaknesses: ✓/✗ and the terms Callable in Lean/New premises are not defined in the caption.
No version, service dependency, latency, or failure condition is encoded.
Light-gray ✗ glyphs provide little redundant labeling in low-contrast or grayscale reproduction.
tables.reusable_pattern: Isolate interface capabilities in a compact matrix with explicit column labels, binary symbols, and a proposal-versus-prior separator; reserve numeric performance for a later table.

tables.label: Table 2

caption.text: Table 2: Performance of LEANHAMMER with different premise selectors on Mathlib-test.

tables.uncertainty: No error bars, intervals, seed dispersion, or repeated-run summaries. Values are point percentages; * denotes an upper bound excluding errors and † denotes a ReProver recall-definition difference.
tables.data_and_statistics: Mathlib-test theorem-level average recall@16/@32 and proof rate (%) for aesop, auto, aesop+auto, full, and cumul. Rows cover None, random forest, MePo, ReProver, LeanPremise small/medium/large, large ∪ MePo, cumulative, cumulative ∪ MePo, and Ground truth. Recall cells are intentionally blank for combination rows where that metric is not reported; they are not zero.
tables.evidence_relation: p.8 §4.2 defines recall@k and proof rate and cites Table 2 for the headline Mathlib comparison. The table connects Figure 1/§3.1 settings and §4.1 model sizes to main results; Table 3 extends full to miniCTX and Table 4 tests component mechanisms.
design_strengths: Two-level grouped headers put retrieval recall and five proof-producing settings on one decision surface.
Baseline, model-size, ensemble, and Ground truth rows are separated by booktabs-like rules.
One-decimal precision and explicit @16/@32, parameter, and setting labels support direct comparison.
Blank combination-row recall cells preserve not-applicable status rather than fabricating zeros.
design_weaknesses: Nine columns and roughly 8.44 pt body text make the table dense; footnotes are about 6.97 pt.
Per-split/theorem denominators, seeds, and result dispersion are absent.
Bold large-model values can look globally best even though Ground truth is higher in some proof-rate columns.
Runtime is reported only in surrounding prose, so this table cannot alone show cost/performance trade-offs.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use grouped headers to align retrieval and end-to-end metrics; separate baselines, model variants, ensembles, and empirical ceilings with horizontal rules; leave inapplicable columns blank and define that choice in a note.

tables.label: Table 3

caption.text: Table 3: Out-of-Mathlib performance of LEANHAMMER on miniCTX-v2-test (Hu et al., 2025) using the large model trained on Mathlib. For other settings than full, see Table 5 of the extended version of this paper (Zhu et al., 2025).

tables.uncertainty: No error bars, intervals, split-level sample counts, or aggregation uncertainty. Values are one-decimal proof-rate percentages; the weighting behind Average is not specified in the table.
tables.data_and_statistics: Full-pipeline proof rate (%) over six miniCTX-v2-test non-Mathlib splits—Carleson, ConNF, FLT, Foundation, HepLean, Seymour—and Average, for None, LeanPremise (large), and Ground truth. Each row has seven reported percentages.
tables.evidence_relation: p.8 §4.2 uses Table 3 for out-of-Mathlib generalization, with None and Ground truth as lower/upper references. The caption points other settings to external Table 5 of Zhu et al. (2025), not to a local appendix.
design_strengths: Six named splits and Average expose cross-domain heterogeneity rather than only one aggregate.
None, large selector, and Ground truth form a clear no-retrieval/observed/ceiling comparison.
Header states full setting and percentage unit; caption gives training domain and model size.
design_weaknesses: Only full is local; other pipeline settings and costs are external Table 5.
Split theorem counts and Average weighting are not shown.
A 0.0 cell has no finer failure category, and the table still relies on the reader knowing the proof-rate definition.
tables.reusable_pattern: Report each real out-of-domain split beside Average, retain None/method/Ground truth rows, and state the training domain and evaluation setting in the caption; link external complete variants explicitly.

tables.label: Table 4

caption.text: Table 4: Ablation study of LEANHAMMER with different training settings on Mathlib-valid.

tables.uncertainty: No error bars, intervals, seeds, or repeated-run summaries. Values are point percentages; surrounding text says proof rate has higher variance than recall but gives no dispersion.
tables.data_and_statistics: Mathlib-valid recall@16/@32 and proof rate (%) for LeanPremise medium, + naive data, − negatives, − loss mask, Ground truth, and Ground truth + naive data. The selector rows report all seven metrics; Ground truth rows leave recall blank because recall is not applicable.
tables.evidence_relation: p.10 §4.4 maps rows to §3.2 hammer-aware extraction, §3.3.1 negative sampling, and masked contrastive loss. It tests those mechanism components after Tables 2–3 establish end-to-end and cross-domain behavior, while preserving the anomalous − loss mask cumul value.
design_strengths: Reuses Table 2 column order so retrieval and proof-rate changes are directly comparable.
A group rule separates selector ablations from Ground truth controls.
The anomalous 38.4 cumul cell remains visible and is explained in adjacent prose rather than removed.
Blank Ground truth recall cells preserve non-applicability.
design_weaknesses: The 9-column table is compressed to roughly 8.97 pt.
Row labels do not define the extraction, negative, and mask operations; readers must return to methods.
No visible dispersion accompanies the higher-variance proof-rate claim, so the anomalous cumul value can be over-interpreted.
tables.reusable_pattern: Keep the main result column contract in the ablation table, change only mechanism rows, retain a Ground truth reference, leave non-applicable cells blank, and explain non-monotone cells next to the table.

cross_object_system.visual_narrative: Figure 1 establishes the method interface; Table 1 isolates usability; Table 2 provides the Mathlib-test headline comparison; Table 3 tests out-of-Mathlib robustness; Table 4 tests extraction/training mechanisms. There are no local appendix objects.
cross_object_system.caption_system: All five captions begin with an unbolded Figure/Table label and descriptive title. Figure 1 supplies the only complete encoding key; Table 3 supplies the strongest setup and external-extension pointer. No caption states the main numerical finding.
cross_object_system.table_header_system: Table 1 uses one capability-header level. Tables 2 and 4 share two-level Recall/Proof-rate headers and monospace pipeline-setting labels. Table 3 uses Proof rate using full (%) over named splits and Average.
cross_object_system.method_result_ablation_link: Figure 1 maps the pipeline stages, Table 1 maps its user-facing interface, Tables 2–3 evaluate the pipeline and generalization, and Table 4 removes the extraction/negative/mask components named in the methods. Cross-references are explicit in the surrounding sections.
cross_object_system.main_appendix_link: The local PDF has no appendix or supplementary objects. Table 3 and §§3.2, 4.2–4.3 point to the external Zhu et al. (2025) extended version for examples, Figure 2a, Table 5, and detailed analyses; those materials are not counted here.
cross_object_system.typography_consistency: PDF-object table fonts combine Nimbus Roman No9 L, Computer Modern Roman/math, and Computer Modern Typewriter at about 8.44–8.97 pt; captions are regular serif. Figure 1 uses an estimated 11–13 pt sans-serif raster label, creating a mild but legible cross-object mismatch.
cross_object_system.color_consistency: Only Figure 1 uses chromatic fills and red/black edges; Tables 2–4 are black/white, while Table 1 adds light-gray crosses. No palette is shared across objects, and Figure 1 color semantics are not repeated by node shape or texture.

most_reusable_patterns: Caption-keyed cross-column pipeline with direct node labels and distinct control/information edges.
Separate capability matrix followed by grouped-header result tables that align retrieval and end-to-end outcomes.
Split-plus-Average robustness table and main-column-contract ablation table with explicit blanks for not-applicable values.
highest_value_objects: Figure 1 for the method interface and information/control-flow contract.
Table 2 for the unified Mathlib headline comparison across selectors, scales, ensembles, and Ground truth.
Table 4 for the mechanism mapping and visible non-monotone ablation cell.
failure_patterns: The sole figure is a 215 ppi raster with no public paper-specific vector source.
All result tables show point percentages without denominators, seeds, repeated-run dispersion, or failure categories.
Captions are mostly descriptive; metric and ablation definitions depend on body text, and Table 3 moves complete variants to an external version.
Figure phase classes rely mainly on color, and Table 1 missingness relies on light-gray crosses, leaving limited redundancy for low-quality or color-deficient reproduction.
final_judgment.one_sentence_visual_strategy: A single cross-column flow diagram establishes the method interface, followed by consistent grouped-header tables for headline comparison, split-level robustness, and mechanism ablation, with booktabs rules and caption pointers carrying the narrative.
